$comment: Committed import manifest for the local-relevant slice of bankai-core's tests/fixtures/dualrun/ corpus (issue zheref/nen#4, §8 import mechanics). Every fixture the source category carries is listed -- included ones under dedupe/, excluded ones with the specific reason nen has no equivalent module for that fixture's own claim. 'nen dev replay' replays only the included set against src/issue/search.ts's normalizeTitle/findCanonical -- the pure decision logic 'nen issue search' absorbs from dedupe_handbook_questions.sh. A fixture is never faked to make the slice bigger.

importMechanics.crlfNormalization: Every imported fixture is re-serialized LF-only (tests/fixtures/dualrun/ itself was already LF; this states the discipline explicitly per §8 rather than assuming it holds).
importMechanics.shortWorkspacePaths: The imported directory is 'tests/fixtures/dualrun-slice/dedupe/', not a path mirroring the source's longer 'tests/fixtures/dualrun/dedupe_handbook_questions.sh/' -- the bankai-core#891 lesson: a long fixture path plus a Windows worktree's own already-long prefix risks MAX_PATH.
importMechanics.perFixtureProvenance: Every imported fixture carries its own 'provenance' object: source repo/tag/sha, the exact source path, an import timestamp, and a recording-host caveat -- the bankai-core#853 lesson that a fixture's recordedAt/URLs/IDs are the RECORDING host's synthetic values, never reproducible facts.

scopeOfThisPass: Only the dedupe_handbook_questions.sh category was evaluated and imported this pass. bankai-core's dualrun/ corpus carries ~45 other script categories (pr_ready_gate.sh, sync-labels.sh, colors_schema_check.sh, changelog_*.sh, the CI/runner-probe scripts, the worktree-session guards, ...); none of them were surveyed for inclusion here. This is a named gap, not a claim of completeness -- see the parent task's final report.

fixtures.reason: Pure findCanonical decision: the older of two same-titled issues stays canonical.
Pure findCanonical decision: order-independence -- the listing order must not change which number wins.
Pure normalizeTitle/findCanonical decision: a blank normalized key never matches anything.
Pure findCanonical decision: the no-op path, one open issue, itself.
Pure findCanonical decision: an unrelated open issue must not capture this one.
Pure findCanonical decision: an empty candidate list is always canonical.
Pure findCanonical decision: the minimum-number rule across 3+ candidates.

Pure normalizeTitle decision: tr's C-locale ASCII-only case fold vs a Unicode-aware one -- ported as src/issue/search.ts's asciiLower(), found and fixed by attempting this exact fixture (see the parent task's final report).

Pure findCanonical decision: the duplicate case, verdict only (the close/comment mechanics that follow it in the script are excluded from the comparison -- nen's issue search never closes anything itself; see the next entry's reasoning, which applies here too).
Pure normalizeTitle decision: punctuation and case fold to the same key.

Pins the SHELL's IFS-tab `read` field-splitting rule when parsing a raw TSV row. nen's parseIssueList (src/issue/search.ts) reads gh's --json output directly; it never parses a raw @tsv stream and has no field-splitting code path to test this against.

Pins the shell's verbatim-storage-of-a-raw-text-field quirk (`best="$num"` keeps a leading space). nen's candidates are typed numbers off parsed JSON, not raw text fields; there is nothing in nen that could carry a leading space through.
Same class as the leading-tab case: pins `IFS=$'\t' read`'s remainder-to-last-field behavior on raw TSV, which nen's JSON-based parseIssueList has no equivalent of.

Tests stdout/stderr interleaving of the SCRIPT's own subprocess calls around a listing warning. nen's issue search reports truncation as a typed field (RecipeResult.truncated), not an interleaved stderr write; the two are not the same mechanism to compare.

Tests the script's own control flow when its close/comment gh calls fail. nen's issue search never closes or comments an issue at all (closing a duplicate stays a human/LLM decision, issue #4's 'stays with the LLM' list) -- there is no corresponding control flow in nen.
Same reasoning as close-failure-aborts-before-the-canonical-comment.

Pins dedupe_handbook_questions.sh's OWN truncation-warning boundary (`[ "$count" -eq 100 ]`, an exact-100 test) and its '::warning::' annotation text. nen's analogous flag lives in a different function (issue/search.ts's runSearch, computed as `>= SEARCH_LIMIT` and reported as a JSON field, not a shell-style annotation) -- comparing the two would be checking two different mechanisms, not verifying one.
Tests the script's own abort-on-listing-failure control flow, which has no equivalent for the same reason as the close/comment-failure cases above.

The companion boundary case to limit-100-warns-that-a-duplicate-may-be-missed (101 rows, silent) -- same exclusion reasoning, and explicitly marked 'UNREACHABLE THROUGH REAL gh' by the fixture's own note besides.

Tests stdout/stderr ordering across the script's three unredirected gh subprocess calls (list, close, comment). nen's issue search makes exactly one call and never closes or comments; there is no multi-call ordering to verify.
